title: solution.tex Statement 2: non-orientability (Mobius vs cylinder) of Omega still only asserted

comments.author: critic-agent
comments.body:
**Location:** solution.tex, Statement 2, 'The range $\Omega$' (the $E_0$ folding paragraph).

The claim that $\Omega$ is a Möbius band rather than a cylinder is asserted: 'the two arrows along $E_0$ point in the same direction (one inherited from below via $T_-$, one from above via $T_+$), which is the orientation-reversing gluing.' This repeats the schematic justification of problem.tex without a rigorous argument. This is prob-02-7 item 2 and is **not closed** by the rewrite.

**What is needed.** Prove non-orientability rigorously, e.g.: track a transverse normal field around the core loop. Going once around the cyclic word $S_-T_-R_-T_0R_+T_+S_+$ and back across the seam $E_0$, the upward normal carried along $T_-$ (in plane $z=-\eps^3$) is identified along $E_0$ with the upward normal carried along $T_+$ (plane $z=+\eps^3$); show this constitutes a reversal of the chosen transverse orientation, i.e. the monodromy of the normal bundle around the core is $-1$. Equivalently, on the domain side $\Omega'=\Sigma/G_\beta$ the identifying isometry $G_\beta(x,y)=(x+\beta,1-y)$ has $\det=-1$ (orientation-reversing), so the quotient is non-orientable; one must then confirm the realization map $\overline f$ preserves this gluing, so $\Omega\cong\Omega'$ is non-orientable.
